title: Uncleanness of liquids
about: Ramchal quotes both ends of this thread and labels them himself: the proof as `הוכחה` (Heb p173, Eng p174) and Rav Huna's reply as `סתירה` (Heb p177, Eng p178). That gives two attested labels and makes the passage usable as a test fixture.
The columns disagree on the second citation: the Hebrew reads `פסחים יח ב` and the English reads "Pesachim 17b". Both are recorded rather than resolved.

units.speaker: R. Eleazar
units.en: Liquids cannot become unclean at all according to Torah law.

anatomy.note: `כל עקר`: no uncleanness for liquids at all — the whole class, denied.

units.speaker: R. Eleazar
units.he: תדע, שהרי העיד יוסי בן יועזר איש צרידה על איל קמצא דכן ועל משקין בית מטבחיא דכן
units.en: Know this, for Yosi ben Yo'ezer of Zeredah testified that the ayil locust is clean and that the liquids of the Temple slaughterhouse are clean.

anatomy.note: If liquids could become unclean by Torah law, the liquids of the Temple slaughterhouse would be unclean; Yosi ben Yo'ezer testified they are clean; so they cannot.

units.speaker: Rav Papa
units.he: אפלו למאן דאמר טמאת משקין דאוריתא – משקי בית מטבחיא הלכתא גמירי לה
units.en: Even according to the one who holds that liquid uncleanness is Torah law, the liquids of the Temple slaughterhouse are a halachah handed down from Sinai.

anatomy.note: The testimony speaks of a special halachah handed down from Sinai, not of liquid uncleanness in general — a different respect, so it proves nothing about the general case.
Rav Papa does not deny the testimony; he denies that it reaches R. Eleazar's claim. The ground is real and the house stands over a gap — Ramchal's `אחיו הוא במצוות` pattern (Eng p132–136).

units.note: Ramchal labels only Rav Huna's reply. `דחיה` is inferred here, on the rule at Heb p185 that a `דחיה` may land on a proof that was brought, not only on a statement.

units.speaker: Rav Huna b. Rav Nassan
units.he: ואלא הא דאמר רבי אלעזר אין טמאה למשקין כל עקר … ואי הלכתא גמירי לה – מי גמרינן מנה
units.en: But R. Eleazar concluded that liquids have no uncleanness at all precisely from Yosi ben Yo'ezer's testimony. If that is a halachah from Sinai, could we derive anything from it?

anatomy.note: If the Temple liquids were a halachah from Sinai, nothing could be derived from them; R. Eleazar did derive from them; so they are not. The same shape as the proof it defends.
The contradiction rests on no verse or testimony of its own, only on the deduction beside this badge: R. Eleazar's derivation is the premise, and a received law yields no derivations (Eng p116).

units.note: Ramchal: `הנה כאן סתר שמועתו של רב פפא לחלוטין` — Rav Papa's statement is absolutely contradicted (Heb p177).
